scenes.narration: In some programs, two fifty five plus one equals zero. Here is why.

scenes.label: what an 8 bit number does at its limit
scenes.narration: An eight bit unsigned number holds values from zero to two fifty five. Add one to the maximum, and it wraps around to zero.
That is called integer overflow. Programs must plan for it, or the counter silently restarts.
